title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (ch. V, 'Algèbre des figures', 1986). L is a set and P(L) its power set. An 'admissible' family Φ ⊂ P(L) is a family of subsets with support |Φ| = ∪Φ, satisfying axioms set up on pp. 5–8; the axioms themselves are not on this page. An 'admissible sub-family' of Φ is a sub-family that is closed (fermée) in Φ: if A ∈ Φ' and B ⊂ A with B ∈ Φ, then B ∈ Φ'. Two admissible families Φ, Ψ are 'compatible' (p. 9) when Φ ∪ Ψ is admissible and both Φ and Ψ are closed in Φ ∪ Ψ. Concretely, for A ∈ Φ, B ∈ Ψ and C ⊂ A ∩ B, C ∈ Φ ⟺ C ∈ Ψ; p. 11 restates this as Φ_{A∩B} = Ψ_{A∩B}.

Top of the page. It finishes the proof of Cor. 2 of p. 9: if Φ, Ψ are compatible, then |Φ| ⊂ |Ψ| iff Φ ⊂ Ψ, and |Φ| = |Ψ| iff Φ = Ψ. The proof reduces to the known case of admissible sub-families of one admissible family (Φ ∪ Ψ), via the 'Scholie p. 7'.

Added Cor. 3. For compatible Φ, Ψ and (finite) admissible sub-families Φ' ≤ Φ, Ψ' ≤ Ψ:
- Φ' ∩ Ψ' is admissible;
- Φ' ∪ Ψ' is an admissible sub-family of Φ ∪ Ψ.
So compatible pairs have meets and joins computed set-theoretically.

Main construction. F is the set of all admissible families in P(L), ordered by Φ ≤ Ψ ⟺ Φ is a closed (admissible) sub-family of Ψ.

C1: F has suprema of all bounded subsets. If Φ_i ≤ Ψ for all i, each Φ_i is closed in Ψ. A union of closed sub-families is closed, so ∪Φ_i is an admissible sub-family of Ψ, and it is the sup. The empty collection has as sup the empty admissible family, the least element. The crossed-out text notes this is the unique Φ with |Φ| = ∅.

The added marginal remark: if Φ, Ψ are compatible, then Σ is compatible with Φ ∪ Ψ iff it is compatible with Φ and with Ψ. Hence compatibility is a binary 'coherence': a family is bounded iff it is pairwise compatible.

Continuation on p. 11:
- The irreducible elements ('multiplicités') are the Φ having a greatest element X, i.e. the principal Φ_X = {Y ∈ Φ | Y ≤ X}.
- Every Φ is the sup of the irreducibles below it.
- Compatibility of F, G reduces to compatibility of their irreducible pieces F_X, G_Y.

In modern terms, Grothendieck is proving that (F, ≤) is a bounded-complete, coherent, prime-algebraic partial order. The irreducibles are complete primes and every element is a join of the primes below it. This is exactly the structure Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel and Winskel isolated as 'prime algebraic coherent partial orders' (equivalently prime event structures / stable domains), and closely related to Girard's coherence spaces. The marginal note speaks of a '"figure de Weil"' and of admissible sub-families; its purpose is unclear.
errors: No real error. In C1, the sup should be checked independent of the chosen bound Ψ. This holds: any other upper bound Ψ' contains each Φ_i as a closed sub-family, hence contains the union as a closed sub-family. The step is implicit, and the corresponding passage of the page is heavily struck through and corrected.

Cor. 3's parenthetical '(parties finies)' and the claim that Φ'∪Ψ' is 'finie' are hard to read. The intended statement is probably that Φ'∪Ψ' is an admissible sub-family of Φ∪Ψ; finiteness is relevant only if Φ', Ψ' are finite.

ideas.what: Poset F of admissible families of subsets ordered by 'closed admissible sub-family'; existence of sups of bounded subsets (bounded completeness), least element = empty family
ideas.modern_name: Bounded-complete (consistently complete) partial order / Scott domain structure

ideas.what: Compatibility is pairwise: Σ compatible with Φ∪Ψ iff compatible with Φ and with Ψ; bounded iff pairwise compatible
ideas.modern_name: Coherence (pairwise consistent ⇒ consistent); coherent domains, coherence spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Plotkin (coherent cpos), Berry (stable domains), Girard (coherence spaces, 1987)

ideas.what: Irreducible elements = families with a greatest element; every element is the join of irreducibles below it (p. 11)
ideas.modern_name: Prime-algebraic domain (complete primes, Φ = ∨ primes ≤ Φ)

ideas.what: Cor 2/3: for compatible families, the support determines the family, and intersections/unions of admissible sub-families are admissible
ideas.modern_name: Lattice of closed (down-closed) sub-families; stability (meets of compatible elements)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'algebra of figures' builds, from admissible families of subsets of a set L, a coherent prime-algebraic partial order. Its 'multiplicités' (principal families Φ_X) play the role of complete primes / events, and compatibility is a binary coherence relation. This is the mathematical core of Winskel's event structures and of Girard's coherence spaces, both from theoretical computer science and developed independently at around the same time (1981–87). The link between Grothendieck's combinatorial–geometric 'figures' and domain theory / event structures has not been noted in the literature.
missed.quote: Σ est compatible avec Φ∪Ψ ssi il l'est avec Φ et avec Ψ … F admet des Sup majorés
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would place this unpublished 1986 chapter among early independent appearances of coherent prime-algebraic domains. It could also suggest reading his 'figures' (possibly linked to the 'figure de Weil' remark) via the event-structure / configuration-space dictionary, e.g. their relation to cubical/simplicial models of concurrency.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary order theory, but its exact shape (bounded-complete, pairwise coherence, every element a join of principal primes) matches prime-algebraic coherent domains, found independently in computer science. The domain-theoretic content is not new; the interest lies in the context and in the unexplored link.
transcription_corrections: 'famille liée [?] (Φ∪Ψ)' is probably 'famille (Φ∪Ψ)', i.e. the sub-families of the admissible family Φ∪Ψ.
Marginal note: possibly 'On a ici un "figure de Weil" des sous-figures admissibles' (very uncertain); the 'Weil' reading is doubtful.
C1 line: 'F admet des Sup majorés' is likely 'F admet des Sup majorés' in the sense of 'sups of bounded (majorées) families'.
Bottom-left margin: 'La Sup de la collection vide ∅ ⊂ F(L) est …' is likely continued by 'la famille vide' / 'Φ telle que |Φ| = ∅'.
